title: Obstacles and Paths of Enterprise Digital Management Transformation
summary: With the rapid development of the digital economy, enterprise digital transformation has become the only way for enterprises. This paper focuses on the study of the dialectical relationship between science and technology and humanities, and explores the obstacles and paths faced by enterprises in the process of digital management transformation, tries to find a relative balance between technology and humanistic value, and realizes high-quality digital transformation for enterprises. The study found that the main reason for the failure of the transformation was the excessive reliance on technological upgrading and the neglect of people's dominant position. When the organization does not agree or accept the change of the enterprise, the enterprise may fail in its transformation. Finally, this paper proposes to build a people-oriented digital transformation path, and suggests that enterprises should start from the four dimensions of upgrading strategic cognition, establishing organizational structure, building digital talents and humanistic care, realizing the deep integration of scientific and technological improvement and humanistic management, and achieve the sustainable development of enterprises and the comprehensive improvement of people.

title: Supply Chain Visibility and End-to-End Traceability: Enhancing Food Safety and Consumer Trust in the Consumer Products Industry
summary: The consumer products industry has prioritized food safety incidents and opaque supply chains, as they are no longer an afterthought for them; it's become a strategic priority. This article discusses the practical benefits for foodborne illness risk reduction, quicker recalls, and consumer-trust restoration that can be achieved through end-to-end supply chain visibility, built on the Internet of Things, distributed ledger technology, and the power of artificial intelligence and machine learning. It suggests a 5-layer reference architecture covering data capture, connectivity, data integration and trust, AI/ML analytics and end-user visibility applications, and outlines AI/ML use cases such as anomaly detection, predictive quality scoring, computer-vision quality control, and graph-based trace-back, plus a “workflow” spanning incident to recall enabling continuous model retraining. The article also examines obstacles to implementation, such as data standardization, integration with legacy systems, and cost, and ends with a vision of digital twins, generative AI, and predictive recall. The tables and diagrams illustrate a comprehensive analysis to provide a structured and evidence-based reference for practitioners and researchers on designing and evaluating modern traceability programs.

title: Bridging the gap between dynamic and ordinary capabilities in digital transformation: a bibliometric and topic modelling analysis
summary: Purpose Digital transformation is a key driver of firm performance, supported by technological adoption, strategic alignment and dynamic capabilities (DC). However, a critical gap remains in the limited understanding of how ordinary capabilities (OC) interact with DC in shaping transformation outcomes. This study aims to map the intellectual structure, methodological trends and capability configurations in research on digital transformation, performance and organisational capabilities. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis combined with Latent Dirichlet Allocation was conducted on 818 articles indexed in Scopus and Web of Science (2015–2024), following and preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses guidelines. The study integrates performance indicators, co-occurrence networks and thematic mapping to identify key research trends and structures. Findings The literature evolves through three phases: emergence, structuring and accelerated growth, with strong geographical concentration in China, the UK and Italy. Results show a shift from technology adoption to understanding how firms lead, integrate and sustain digital transformation for performance. While digital, innovation, learning, managerial and cultural capabilities dominate, OC remain largely absent, highlighting a significant gap. Originality/value This study emphasises the importance of integrating dynamic and OC to better explain digital transformation and performance. It proposes an integrative capability perspective and calls for longitudinal research to capture capability co-evolution over time.

title: Intelligent Financial Analytics by using AI and Machine Learning in Fintech.
summary: Recent advancements in the field of Financial Technology along with Machine Learning have transfigured the financial ecosystem by enhancing the business intelligence solutions that are driven by large scale financial data. Today, financial organizations are increasingly using Machine learning models for extensive financial data analysis in order to produce meaningful insights. This further enhances the operational effectiveness and minimizes the risk and also help in taking correct decisions. Present work explores the manner by which machine learning and advancements in Fintech sway business intelligence. This emphasizes fraud-detection, risk valuation, algorithmic trade-off and economic decision making. This research examines the way by which complex financial data is analysed by machine learning algorithms for predicting financial trends, detecting frauds, assessing risks and supporting automated trading. title: The Impact of Institutional Pressures on the Implementation of Environmental Management Accounting: A Case Study of Listed Companies in Vietnam
summary: This study employs Institutional Theory to explain the impact of coercive, mimetic, and normative pressures on the implementation of Environmental Management Accounting (EMA) in listed companies in Vietnam. Through a qualitative case study methodology in three representative companies from high-environmental-impact industries, combining semi structured interviews with key managers and documentary analysis, the study deeply explores the drivers and mechanisms behind EMA adoption. The findings reveal that EMA implementation is not the product of a single pressure but a complex interplay of all three. Coercive pressure serves as a fundamental driver, initiating initial compliance activities. Meanwhile, mimetic pressure helps disseminate best practices, and normative pressure from supply chains, investors, and leadership vision is the most powerful driver, promoting the substantive integration of EMA into business strategy. The study not only illuminates an evolutionary path of EMA adoption in an emerging economy—from passive compliance to strategic integration—but also offers significant implications for managers in using EMA as a competitive tool and for policymakers in fostering an institutional environment conducive to sustainable development.

title: Environmental Accounting Disclosure and Value Creation of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: Value creation in emerging markets remains severely constrained by economic volatility, governance weaknesses and inconsistent sustainability practices, and these challenges are further intensified by limited transparency in environmental reporting, making it difficult for investors to assess firms’ long-term resilience and financial prospects. Although environmental accounting disclosure has been increasingly recognized as a potential driver of value, prior studies have not adequately disaggregated disclosure into its specific components (greenhouse gas intensity, waste management disclosure, water usage disclosure and renewable energy disclosure) thereby leaving a gap in understanding how each dimension individually contributed to value creation in Nigeria’s manufacturing sector. This study filled that gap by analyzing panel data from 14 listed industrial goods firms between 2015 and 2024 using a fixed-effects model with Driscoll–Kraay robust standard errors. The results revealed that greenhouse gas intensity (β = 7.032, p < 0.05), waste management disclosure (β = 2.053, p < 0.05) and water usage disclosure (β = 1.981, p < 0.01) exert significant positive effects on Earnings Per Share (EPS), suggesting that operational efficiency and transparent resource stewardship enhance value creation. Conversely, renewable energy disclosure showed a significant negative effect (β = 0.196, p < 0.05), reflecting the short-term cost implications of renewable energy adoption. Firm size positively influenced value creation (β = 0.360, p < 0.01), while firm age exhibited a negative effect (β = –0.714, p < 0.05). The model is significant (Prob > F = 0.0051) with a within R² of 0.1452, confirming that environmental disclosure practices partly explain variationsin firm value. Based on these findings, the study recommended that firms should strengthen structured waste and water disclosure systems, adopt phased and financially sustainable renewable-energy strategies, and improve emissions reporting credibility through verification mechanisms. Regulators should enforce sector-specific disclosure standards, while policymakers should introduce incentives that reduce the financial burden associated with environmental transitions and enhance the comparability and reliability of sustainability disclosures.

title: Digital Transformation in University Libraries: A Case Study of Digital Archiving Project at the Central Library in Basra University
summary: This study aims to explore the digital transformations that may occur in university libraries. The study focus on a case study of a Digital Archiving Project implemented at the Central Library of Basra University in Iraq in collaboration with the Digital Information Center at the AL-Abbas Holy Shrine Library. This study is the first of its type to present a comprehensive overview of the project’s objectives methodologies and results. The aim is to assess the impact of the transition form traditional archiving practices to digital applications. This is particularly important in the field of theses and dissertations. Based on project documents reports from participating institutions and observations on the archiving processes software used, digitization techniques, and data management processes, a qualitative case study approach was employed. The project resulted in easier access to academic content reduced the administrative workload, and reduced the risk of data loss and damage. Additionally, long-term preservation plans and a frequent backup strategy have ensured the sustainability and accessibility of digital content. The project not only improved operational functions but has also contributed significantly to preserving the legacy of Iraqi academics and has strengthened the role of university libraries in the development of digital libraries. All of this presents an important opportunity for colleges and universities as part of their efforts to develop their information services. By creating a workable and scalable operational model this case study shows not only how digital transformation can enrich the national infrastructure for scientific research, but also how libraries should strategically navigate the digital environment.

title: Audit Attributes and Earnings Quality of Quoted Oil and Gas Firms in Nigeria
summary: The oil and gas sector of the Nigerian economy is a major source of revenue for the nation, thus financial statement disclosed in this sector is crucial to retain investors’ confidence. However, there have been growing concern as the sector has been reporting cases of earnings manipulations despite the regulatory reforms. The study was motivated by the persistent cases of audit failures, earnings manipulation and financial misreporting in the oil and gas sector in Nigeria which has eroded investors’ confidence and credibility of financial disclosures. It is on this basis that the study examined the effect of audit attributes on earnings quality of quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria from 2014 to 2024. The study was anchored on agency, signaling and stakeholder theory. Secondary data were extracted from the audited annual reports of quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria. Earnings quality being the dependent variable was measured by discretionary accruals derived using the modified Jones model, while audit attributes, the independent variable was measured by audit firm fees (AFS), audit firm size (AFZ), audit firm rotation (AFR), audit report timeliness (ART) and audit committee financial expertise (ACX) with firm size as control variable. Panel data were analyzed using the generalized linear model (GLM) estimation technique. The findings revealed that AFS exert positive significant effect on earnings quality. AFZ and ACX had positive but statistically insignificant effect on earnings quality. Conversely, AFR and ART displayed negative but insignificant effect on earnings quality of quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria. The study concludes that audit attributes influence earnings quality of quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria but their influence varies in direction and magnitude. The study recommends that Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria (FRCN) should collaborate with professional bodies such as ICAN, ANAN, etc. to develop a standardized benchmark audit fees charged by external auditors so as to discourage charging of fees that threatens auditor objectivity in order to ensure transparency. Also, SEC should set deadlines for publication of audited reports to enhance investors’ confidence and timeliness of information.

title: When big data meets green finance: how cross-domain policy coordination promotes green collaborative innovation in Chinese cities
summary: Using panel data for 272 Chinese cities from 2010 to 2022, this study employs the regression control method combined with Lasso and a Lasso-based synthetic control method to estimate the effect of the joint implementation of the National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones (NBDCPZ) and the Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones (GFRIPZ) on intercity green collaborative innovation (GCI), with Guangzhou as the treated city. Baseline estimates show that cross-domain policy coordination (CDPC) promotes Guangzhou’s intercity GCI. The finding is robust to placebo tests and alternative estimators, donor pools, covariate sets, outcome measures, sample periods, and estimation frameworks and is further supported by an alternative treated-city analysis using Guiyang. Mechanism analysis indicates that CDPC promotes intercity GCI by improving access to finance and fostering computing infrastructure development. The CDPC effect exceeds either standalone-policy benchmark under both estimators, while sequencing analysis shows an additional positive effect from adding GFRIPZ after NBDCPZ. The findings support closer coordination between digital-development and green-finance policies to strengthen intercity GCI.

title: Is Blockchain Technology Reshaping Traceability and Supply Chain Transparency in Agri-Food Systems? Learning from Generation Z Consumers in Malaysia
summary: With increasing concerns over food safety, fraud, and information asymmetry in global food supply chains, improving transparency has become a key challenge for modern agricultural systems. Traditional supply chains often lack visibility, leading to fragmented data, reduced consumer trust, and difficulties in verifying food product information. Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for enabling decentralised and tamper-resistant data sharing across supply networks. However, despite its theoretical potential, empirical evidence remains limited regarding how blockchain adoption enhances transparency through specific operational mechanisms, such as traceability. Therefore, this study investigates the role of blockchain adoption in improving traceability and strengthening supply chain transparency within agri-food systems. Data were collected from Generation Z university students in Malaysia, selected due to their familiarity with digital technologies and heightened awareness of food sourcing issues. The study is based on a total of 253 usable responses analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics 27, employing reliability analysis, Exploratory Factor Analysis, Pearson correlation, multiple regression analysis, and the PROCESS Macro Model 4 with 5000 bootstrap resamples for mediation testing. The findings indicate that blockchain adoption is significantly and positively associated with traceability, which in turn is positively associated with overall supply chain transparency. Furthermore, traceability is found to act as a mediating factor, serving as the key mechanism through which blockchain generates transparency outcomes, via an indirect-only mediation pathway. Thus, based on this premise, it is evident that blockchain alone is not sufficient unless integrated with effective traceability systems, highlighting the importance of aligning digital infrastructure with physical supply chain processes to strengthen trust and resilience in agricultural systems.

title: INSTITUTIONAL AND FINANCIAL FACTORS AFFECTING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ISLAMIC FINANCE PRINCIPLES IN COMMERCIAL BANKS OF UZBEKISTAN
summary: This thesis analyzes the key institutional and financial factors affecting the implementation of Islamic finance principles in commercial banks of Uzbekistan. Integrating Islamic financial services into the banking system is not limited to offering new financial products but also requires an appropriate regulatory and legal framework, mechanisms for ensuring Sharia compliance, corporate governance, accounting and auditing, risk management, and the development of qualified human resources. At the same time, banks’ capital and liquidity positions, access to Islamic financing sources, asset and liability management mechanisms, and costs associated with introducing new products are particularly important as financial factors. The study examines the interrelationship between institutional and financial factors through a systematic approach and substantiates the need to assess them as factors that either facilitate or constrain the implementation of Islamic finance principles. It also highlights the importance of maintaining a balance between institutional infrastructure and financial capacity for the sustainable development of Islamic financial services in commercial banks. The findings may serve as a basis for identifying priority areas for the gradual implementation of Islamic finance principles in commercial banks of Uzbekistan and developing scientific and practical approaches aimed at improving banks’ readiness for transformation.

title: De-Dollarization and the Collapse of the Petrodollar Order: A Meta-Analysis of Iran’s Currency Shift and its Disruptive Effects on Global Trade, Accounting Profitability, and Financial Power Structures
summary: De-dollarisation and the transformation of the petrodollar order have generated increasing debate concerning the future of global trade, corporate financial performance and international financial power. However, existing literature remains fragmented across monetary economics, international trade, accounting and corporate finance. This study addresses this gap by integrating these dimensions to examine the disruptive implications of Iran’s currency shift for global trade, accounting profitability and financial power structures. A meta-analysis of 37 peer-reviewed studies retrieved from CrossRef, Semantic Scholar and Google Scholar were conducted using a structured review matrix, effect-size calculation, heterogeneity assessment, subgroup analysis and sensitivity testing. The findings identify three interconnected themes: geopolitical environment, financial-system adaptability, and institutional and regulatory frameworks. Geopolitical tensions and sanctions encourage alternative trade and payment arrangements, while financial-system adaptability determines resilience to currency-related risks. Strong institutional and regulatory frameworks further support transparent reporting, financial stability and corporate adaptation. The study contributes theoretically by integrating monetary, geopolitical and accounting perspectives and practically by informing policymakers and financial managers navigating an increasingly diversified international monetary system.

title: Digital Transformation of Educational Administrative Services in an Archipelagic Region: A Case Study of the Buru Regency Education Branch Office
summary: Digital transformation can reduce administrative distance in archipelagic regions, but digital channels do not automatically produce integrated public services. This study analyzes the transformation of educational administrative services at the Buru Regency Education Branch Office, Maluku Province, Indonesia. A qualitative documentary case-study design was applied to publicly verifiable institutional documents and digital-service evidence available through August 2026. The analysis used five dimensions: governance and leadership, service-process transformation, digital infrastructure, human-resource competence and work culture, and system/data integration, interpreted through public-value and administrative-burden perspectives. The results show that the Branch Office has established a digital presence through its institutional website, electronic communication, education-data administration, and participation in digital infrastructure mapping. Provincial and national platforms, including Lawamena Satu Data Maluku, further expand the enabling ecosystem. However, evidence of end-to-end transactions, service tracking, interoperable workflows, standardized response times, and locally documented platform use remains limited. The study concludes that the next transformation stage requires service-process standardization, one-door service orchestration, data governance, distributed digital competence, traceability, security, and assisted channels for schools facing connectivity constraints.

title: Pengaruh Struktur Modal, Likuiditas, dan Profitabilitas terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Perusahaan Non-Perbankan LQ45
summary: Firm value served as a primary reflection of overall corporate performance and market perception, which was heavily influenced by underlying financial decisions. In modern capital markets, maintaining an optimal balance between financing risks and asset efficiency remained a critical challenge for large-scale enterprises listed on benchmark indices like the LQ45. This study aimed to examine the empirical effect of capital structure, liquidity, and profitability on firm value among non-banking companies consistently listed on the LQ45 Index during the 2020–2024 period. Employing a quantitative associative approach with purposive sampling, a final dataset of 17 companies yielding 85 balanced panel observations was analyzed using panel data regression, preceded by model selection procedures through the Chow and Hausman tests which established the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) as the optimal specification. The empirical results demonstrated that while capital structure (DER) and liquidity (CR) exhibited a negative yet statistically insignificant effect, profitability (ROE) showed a positive but statistically insignificant effect on firm value (PBV). Nevertheless, all independent variables simultaneously exerted a significant joint influence on firm value. These findings aligned with the Efficient Market Theory (semi-strong form), indicating that public fundamental indicators had been priced-in by market participants. This research contributed valuable insights to corporate finance literature by highlighting that financial ratios were evaluated holistically by investors rather than in isolation, suggesting that corporate management needed to focus on comprehensive long-term value creation strategies, while future studies were encouraged to incorporate broader external or macroeconomic indicators.

title: Accounting-Based Performance Measures and Market Valuation of Industrial Goods Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of accounting-based performance measures on the market valuation of firms listed in the industrial goods sector of the Nigerian Exchange Group. The study specifically assessed the effect of Return on Equity (ROE) and Net Asset Value per Share (NAVPS) on share price. An ex post facto research design was adopted, utilizing secondary data obtained from the published annual financial reports of eleven (11) industrial goods firms covering the period 2019 to 2024. Given the manageable size of the population, a census approach was employed. Panel regression analysis and descriptive statistics were used to analyze the data. Share Price (SP) served as the proxy for market valuation, while ROE and NAVPS were used as independent variables. The findings revealed that ROE has a positive and statistically significant effect on share price (β = 332.92, p < 0.05), indicating that higher profitability enhances market valuation. NAVPS, however, exhibited a negative and statistically significant effect on share price (β = -118.65, p < 0.05), suggesting that book value-based measures may not strongly drive investor pricing decisions within the sector. The study concludes that accounting-based performance measures are value relevant in the industrial goods sector, with profitability indicators playing a more dominant role than asset-based measures in determining market valuation.

title: The Influence of Direct Market Access on Profit Margins, Supply Chain Efficiency, and Economic Resilience for Small-Scale Dairy Farmers of Asian Country
summary: This study investigates the impact of Direct Market Access (DMA) on the economic results of Small-Scale Dairy Farmers (SSDF) in Gujarat, India. Specifically, it explores how DMA impacts Profit Margins (PM), Supply Chain Efficiency (SSE), and Economic Resilience (ER), compared to Traditional Market Access (TMA), which intermediaries dominate. A total of 248 SSDF participated in the study, with data collected through structured surveys and financial records. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, including t-tests, ANOVA, and Multiple Regression (MR), were employed to assess the relationships between Market Access Type (MAT) and Key Economic Indicators. The results show that farmers using DMA reported significantly higher PM (Mean=₹. 29,123) than those using TMA (Mean=₹. 26,347). The DMA is better SSE by reducing transportation costs, time to market, and product wastage, with a significant difference in efficiency scores (t=4.02, p=0.001). The Farm Size (FS), Education Level (EL), and Years of Experience (YoE) considerably affect agricultural results. Large farms mean there are more scale efficiencies because a farm is a significant operation with many resources to utilize. Education increases farmers' understanding, enhances new technologies, and encourages them to adopt performance management. YoE results in more effective decisions based on practical knowledge, risk management, and an adaptive approach. All these factors are consistent; for example, educated farmers with suitable experience and large farms have the best chance of adopting new methods and maximizing returns and productivity. These improvements create tenacity, sustainability, and effectiveness in farming businesses. DMA enhanced ER, enabling farmers to withstand market fluctuations better and maintain stable incomes. Key factors such as FS, EL, and YoE further influenced these outcomes, with larger and more educated farmers benefiting more from DMA. The study concludes that DMA is a viable strategy for improving the economic sustainability of SSDF. However, addressing gender disparities and providing education and capacity-building initiatives are essential for ensuring that all farmers can fully benefit from DMA. These findings offer essential identifications for policymakers, farmer cooperatives, and development organizations focused on enhancing the incomes of SSDF.

title: Islamic financial inclusion, fintech and poverty reduction: a dynamic panel analysis from a newly constructed provincial index in Indonesia
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop a provincial-level Islamic Financial Inclusion Index (IFII) for Indonesia and empirically examine the relationship between Islamic financial inclusion, fintech development and poverty reduction across 33 provinces from 2015 to 2023. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-method approach is used. The IFII integrates Islamic banking, Islamic microfinance and Islamic social finance across accessibility, availability and usage, using Delphi-based weighting and geometric mean aggregation. The empirical analysis applies the two-step System Generalized Method of Moments to account for poverty persistence, potential endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity. An alternative lagged specification is used as a robustness check. Findings The direct associations of Islamic financial inclusion and fintech development with poverty reduction are statistically insignificant. However, their interaction is negative and statistically significant, indicating that the relationship between Islamic financial inclusion and poverty is conditional on fintech development. Marginal-effects analysis shows that this association becomes negative and statistically significant at relatively high levels of fintech development. The alternative lagged specification produces a similar negative interaction. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of integrating Islamic financial institutions, Islamic social finance and digital financial development. Policymakers should strengthen institutional coordination, digital infrastructure and digital and Islamic financial literacy, particularly in underserved provinces in Indonesia. Originality/value This study constructs a new multidimensional index, the Islamic IFII, at the provincial level and presents dynamic evidence showing that the relationship between Sharia financial inclusion and poverty reduction varies systematically with the development of fintech.

title: Financial Technology Adoption and Deposit Money Bank Operational Performance in Nigeria
summary: The rapid expansion of Financial Technology (FinTech) has fundamentally altered the structure and operations of banking systems worldwide, raising critical questions about its implications for traditional banks in emerging economies. This study examines the effect of FinTech adoption on the operational efficiency, profitability, and customer service delivery of Nigerian commercial banks. Employing a quantitative ex-post facto research design, the study utilises panel data from all commercial banks licensed in Nigeria over the period 2013–2025. FinTech adoption is proxied by digital transaction activity, while bank performance is measured using indicators of operational efficiency, profitability, and service delivery. Panel regression techniques are applied within the Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE) framework to account for firm-level and macroeconomic influences. The findings reveal that FinTech adoption has a positive and statistically significant effect on operational efficiency, indicating that digital technologies enhance process automation and cost management in Nigerian banks. FinTech adoption also positively influences profitability, although the magnitude of this effect is relatively moderate, reflecting the offsetting impact of high implementation costs and competitive pressure from non bank FinTech firms. Furthermore, the results show a strong and significant relationship between FinTech penetration and customer service delivery, underscoring the central role of digital platforms in reshaping customer–bank interactions. Overall, the study concludes that FinTech is not displacing traditional banks in Nigeria but is instead driving a process of operational transformation and strategic adaptation. The findings offer important implications for bank management and financial regulators seeking to balance innovation, competitiveness, and financial stability in the digital era.

title: From shop to classroom: Using charity volunteering to inform community-engaged accounting education
summary: Accounting Information Systems (AIS) can appear highly procedural when taught through structured textbook content, whereas organisational practices require students to exercise judgement in situations featuring ambiguity, competing objectives, and resource constraints. This paper reflects on an emerging teaching initiative that translates charity volunteering experience into an accounting teaching case, which aims at creating an authentic learning context. Drawing on approximately 18 hours of volunteering in a charity vintage shop in Northern Ireland, the United Kingdom, the initiative uses situated observations to identify AIS issues embedded in everyday retail practice. Four pedagogically useful tensions emerged: trust versus control, charity mission versus financial resilience, central guidance versus local reality, and circularity versus traceability. These tensions are being developed into a teaching case for the module titled Accounting Information Systems and Auditing, where students can learn relevant subject knowledge by mapping processes, diagnosing risks, and recommending proportionate improvements. The paper argues that educators’ own community engagement can provide practical insights into authentic, community-engaged curriculum development, while recognising that reciprocal partnership and classroom evaluation remain important next steps.

title: UED Reconstruction Programme — Paper 1: Energetic Reconstruction of Classical Mechanics
summary: This paper establishes the mechanical base layer of the UED Reconstruction Programme by reconstructing classical mechanics in an explicitly energetic and consequential language without altering its verified empirical predictions. Conservative mechanical interaction is represented through configurational energy U(q)U(q), with the local generalized energetic drive defined by QE=−∂U/∂qQ_E=-\partial U/\partial q. Combined with inertial response, this recovers the classical Lagrange equation and, in Cartesian constant-mass form, Mq¨=−∇U+QncM\ddot q=-\nabla U+Q_{nc}. The same structure yields work-energy conservation, impulse-momentum response, equilibrium, Hessian-based local stability, normal-mode dynamics, persistence barriers, and explicit mechanical-energy loss under linear damping. A mass-spring-damper system provides technology-level validation. The reconstruction also establishes an important negative result for the wider programme: energy is not identical to active Delta, because inertial motion can persist without a continuing energetic gradient. Paper 1 therefore does not propose new mechanics. Its role is to establish the classical limit, variable discipline, energy accounting, persistence criteria, and no-patch methodology that later UED papers must recover or explicitly generalize.

title: influence of ESG information and digital communication on Vietnamese consumers’ building material choices
summary: This study examines the influence of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) information and digital communication on Vietnamese consumers’ building material choices. A quantitative research design was employed using survey data from 326 consumers who had purchased, considered purchasing, or participated in decisions related to building materials. The measurement scales were assessed using Cronbach’s alpha and exploratory factor analysis, followed by multiple linear regression to test the proposed hypotheses. The results indicate that both ESG information and digital communication have positive and statistically significant effects on consumers’ building material choices. ESG information has a stronger influence (? = 0.421) than digital communication (? = 0.286), while the model explains 37.5% of the variance in consumer choice. The findings extend ESG-oriented consumer research to the building-material sector and highlight the importance of providing credible sustainability information through effective digital channels. The study provides practical implications for manufacturers, distributors, and marketers seeking to promote sustainable building-material consumption in Vietnam.

title: UED Reconstruction Programme — Paper 2: Ripple Dynamics in SVE
summary: Paper 2 develops the first non-classical dynamical layer of the UED Reconstruction Programme: a minimal local-coupling description of ripple dynamics in Structured Vacuum Energy (SVE). Rather than assuming a mechanical wave, electromagnetic field, particle stream, or moving medium, the reconstruction introduces two operational quantities: a dimensionless local ripple-state departure R(x,t)R(\mathbf{x},t) and a spatial coupling flux JR(x,t)\mathbf{J}_R(\mathbf{x},t). Local state accounting together with finite coupling-flux adaptation generates a damped hyperbolic ripple equation rather than assuming one in advance. The resulting framework yields finite characteristic front speed, attenuation, complex dispersion, a diffusion limit, anisotropic response, geometric spreading, linear superposition, interface reflection and transmission, bounded-domain resonance, and a passive-response stability result. It requires no bulk SVE velocity, making a globally still reference substrate mathematically compatible with locally propagating consequences. Front delay, phase delay, group delay, local relaxation, and Alignment Threshold Time (ATT) are explicitly separated. The model remains conditional: RR has no absolute substrate-energy calibration, vRv_R is not identified with the optical constant cc, and its constitutive coefficients require independent empirical measurement.

title: Auditing Memory Attribution in a Trading-Agent Replay
summary: This paper presents a paired attribution audit of teacher-forced trading-agent replays using a frozen SPY historical replay. The study examines whether observed action changes can be attributed to retrieved return content rather than to surrounding risk wording, recommendations, or authority framing. Across three experiments, surrounding guidance reproduced the tested Llama action shifts, while the tested negative-only versus balanced return-composition substitutions produced no observed action switches. These results are configuration-specific and do not establish that retrieved facts were ignored. The task lacked an objective evidence-dependent decision rule, and the historical records do not provide a complete raw-attempt stream. The paper therefore treats the findings as a bounded attribution audit and identifies the evidence-use positive control required for stronger conclusions. No live trading, investment recommendation, or general claim about language-model memory is made.

title: The Knowledge and Skills Gap: Challenges in Training and Self Training in Environmental Accounting for Vietnam's Accounting Workforce
summary: This study aims to systematize and analyze the challenges in training and self-training, thereby identifying the "knowledge and skills gap" in environmental accounting (EA) among the accounting workforce in Vietnam. Using desk research and content analysis of diverse secondary data such as training curricula, professional documents, and corporate reports, the findings confirm the existence of a profound competency gap. This gap stems from both the "supply" side (formal and professional training systems that lack depth and are slow to update) and the "demand" side (limited awareness and requirements from businesses). Consequently, the study provides a scientific basis for proposing policy implications and synergistic solutions for educational institutions, professional associations, and regulatory bodies to enhance the quality of the accounting workforce, meeting the urgent demands of the green economy and international integration.

title: Digital Capability of Manufacturing Enterprises
summary: Promoting the digital transformation of the manufacturing industry has become a focus for advancing the digital economy alongside the real economy. However, current research has not identified the key dimensions of digital capability in manufacturing enterprises, and there is a lack of well-developed measurement scales. This study addresses this gap by conducting semi-structured interviews and analyzing secondary data from 45 middle and senior managers across 13 manufacturing enterprises. Using procedural grounded theory, it explores the key dimensions of digital capability in these enterprises, which include digital perception capability, digital business capability, and digital co-creation capability. Based on these findings, the study developed a measurement scale consisting of three dimensions and 20 items, validated through exploratory factor analysis (N=268) and confirmatory factor analysis (N=345). This research provides an effective tool for measuring the digital capability of manufacturing enterprises and offers practical insights for further empirical studies in this area.

title: Analysis of The Implementation of The Government Financial Accounting System In Improving The Quality of Local Government Financial Statements: a Case Study of The Prabumulih City Government
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation of the government financial accounting system in improving the quality of the Local Government Financial Statements of Prabumulih City. A qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and a literature review. The data were analyzed through the stages of data collection, data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that the Regional Government Information System of the Republic of Indonesia (SIPD-RI) has been implemented effectively and in an integrated manner within the Prabumulih City Government. SIPD-RI integrates the planning, budgeting, financial administration, and financial reporting processes into a centralized database, thereby reducing the risk of duplicate records and improving information consistency. The implementation of the system also supports the quality of the Prabumulih City Government's financial statements. The financial information presented fulfills the qualitative characteristics of financial statements stipulated in Government Regulation Number 71 of 2010 concerning Government Accounting Standards, namely relevance, reliability, comparability, and understandability. Therefore, the implementation of SIPD-RI plays an important role in supporting more effective, integrated, transparent, and accountable regional financial management.

title: Autonomous Logistics in the Context of Sustainability and Digitalisation: A Systematic Review
summary: Increasing global competition has expanded the role of logistics within supply chains and heightened its importance. The awareness raised by the environmental, social and economic challenges faced has led to the widespread global acceptance of a sustainability approach that calls for the use of resources with due regard for the needs of future generations. This has highlighted the need to reorganise logistics activities – which, by their very nature, have a significant environmental impact – with sustainability in mind. As in all other sectors, the opportunities offered by advancing technology are driving digital transformation in logistics. In line with all these developments, autonomous logistics—one of the emerging trends in the sector—is finding an increasingly broad scope of application. This study aims to examine the concept of autonomous logistics within the context of sustainability and digitalisation. To this end, a systematic review was conducted using the PRISMA approach. As part of the research, a search was carried out in the Web of Science and Scopus databases, resulting in the analysis of 20 studies deemed suitable. Based on the qualitative analysis of the findings, it can be said that the literature reveals a strong relationship between autonomous logistics and digitalisation, and its supportive effect on sustainable logistics transformation.

title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF SOCIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND SUSTAINABLE PROCUREMENT PRACTICES ON FINANCIAL AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN DANGOTE CEMENT
summary: The cement sector makes a sizable contribution to global carbon emissions, sustainability practices in this sector are essential for preserving the environment. The largest cement manufacturer in Nigeria, Dangote Cement PLC, has made several sustainability commitments as part of its corporate strategy. However, there hasn't been enough research done on how these practices affect corporate success and environmental preservation in Lagos State, Nigeria. The goal of this study is to evaluate how well Dangote Cement PLC's sustainability initiatives are working in Lagos State, Nigeria. This study is important because it has the potential to guide corporate decisions and inform legislation regarding sustainable practices in the cement sector, particularly in developing nations. The research findings might also contribute to the body of knowledge on corporate social responsibility and sustainability in high-emission industries. An extensive investigation of Dangote Cement's sustainability practices, their effects on the environment, and how they affect the company's financial success are all part of the research's content. The study will also examine how business activities strike a balance between economic, environmental, and social sustainability.

title: El precio del desencanto: reacción bursátil a los anuncios de beneficios de empresas ESG
summary: El objetivo de este trabajo es determinar si las empresas con alta calificación ambiental, social y de gobernanza (ESG) registran rendimientos anormales negativos alrededor de sus anuncios trimestrales de beneficios, una vez agotado el impulso de expectativas que sostuvo su valuación previa. El marco teórico distingue entre rendimiento esperado y realizado: si el desempeño superior de los activos verdes obedeció a revisiones al alza no anticipadas en la preocupación por la sostenibilidad, la detención de ese flujo implica la convergencia del rendimiento realizado hacia un nivel esperado menor, proceso denominado aquí desencanto. La metodología es un estudio de eventos aplicado a doscientos anuncios empresa-trimestre de las veinticinco empresas de mayor capitalización del índice S&P 500 ESG entre 2023 y 2025; los rendimientos anormales se estiman con el modelo de mercado sobre una ventana de estimación de ochenta días y se acumulan en ventanas de evento de (-4, +6) y (-17, +17) días, con inferencia de una cola agrupada por empresa. El rendimiento anormal acumulado resulta negativo en ambas ventanas: -2.429% en la estrecha y -1.038% en la amplia. El día del anuncio no presenta reacción significativa y la corrección se concentra en t = -4 y en t = +6. Se concluye que el ajuste de precios no ocurre en el momento de la revelación sino de forma difusa antes y después de ella, patrón consistente con una repreciación de expectativas. La ausencia de un grupo de control no ESG acota la evidencia a un plano descriptivo.

title: FinTech-driven financial inclusion and market efficiency in developing countries: Digital access, financial intermediation, developmental outcomes and institutional conditions
summary: This paper examines the relationship between FinTech, financial inclusion and market efficiency in developing countries through a structured review of the recent literature. The analysis focuses on three main dimensions: the contribution of digital financial technologies to the expansion of financial inclusion, their effects on the efficiency and organization of financial markets, and their broader developmental, distributive and institutional consequences. The reviewed studies show that mobile money, digital payments, alternative lending platforms and data-driven financial services can reduce geographical, informational and transaction-cost barriers that limit access to conventional financial systems. FinTech can also improve credit allocation, accelerate financial transactions and strengthen competition and complementarity between traditional banks and technological providers. However, these effects remain conditional on digital infrastructure, financial literacy, institutional quality, regulation and users’ capacity to adopt and use digital services effectively. The literature further indicates that digital financial inclusion can support economic growth, entrepreneurship, household welfare and formalization, while also generating risks related to financial vulnerability, data governance, cybersecurity, market concentration and unequal access. The paper concludes that FinTech can contribute to more inclusive and efficient financial systems when technological innovation is accompanied by appropriate institutional, regulatory and social conditions

title: Voluntary disclosure, banking stability, and AI-augmented forensic accounting: an exploratory econometric and machine-learning study of Palestinian banks
summary: Introduction Information asymmetry between bank managers and external stakeholders is a common relationship between financial-statement fraud and banking instability. Methods This study combines an AI-augmented forensic accounting framework with voluntary disclosure, banking stability indicators, and exploratory machine learning (ML) approaches. The study integrates fixed-effects regression with Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Isolation Forest, and SHAP-based explainability using panel data from the whole population of seven banks listed on the Palestine Exchange (2019–2025). Results According to the econometric results, there is a conditional rather than a uniform relationship between voluntary disclosure and financial stability, with variation by bank size, age, and leverage. Additionally, the exploratory machine-learning analyses indicate that nonlinear approaches could help find unusual bank-year records and instability-risk patterns that are not fully captured by traditional linear models. SHAP analysis enhanced the interpretability of model classifications, and ensemble approaches outperformed Logistic Regression in cross-validation within this small sample. The machine-learning results are considered as exploratory proof-of-concept evidence rather than externally confirmed predictive outcomes due to the small sample size and lack of independently verified fraud labels. Discussion Overall, the study shows how AI-augmented forensic accounting can enhance supervisory prioritization, instability-risk screening, and the expert assessment of anomalous observations in institutionally unstable banking contexts, thereby complementing traditional econometric analysis.

title: WHISTLEBLOWING MECHANISMS IN PROCUREMENT FRAUD CASES: A CONCEPTUAL AND ANALYTICAL STUDY OF DETECTION, REPORTING, AND INSTITUTIONAL RESPONSE
summary: Procurement fraud remains one of the most persistent threats to value-for-money, transparency, and institutional integrity in both public and private sector supply chains. Conventional internal controls—audits, segregation of duties, and approval hierarchies—have repeatedly proven insufficient to detect collusive practices such as bid-rigging, bribery, conflict of interest, and contract inflation, largely because these schemes are deliberately concealed by insiders who understand the control environment. Whistleblowing has therefore emerged as one of the most effective detection mechanisms available to organisations, frequently outperforming formal audit and control systems in uncovering fraud. This paper undertakes a conceptual and analytical review of whistleblowing mechanisms as tools for detecting and deterring procurement fraud. It examines the theoretical foundations of whistleblowing behaviour, the institutional and legal frameworks that support or inhibit disclosure, the organisational and psychological barriers that discourage employees and third parties from reporting wrongdoing, and the design features that distinguish effective whistleblowing systems from symbolic or dysfunctional ones. Drawing on secondary literature, international case evidence, and comparative regulatory frameworks, the paper argues that the effectiveness of whistleblowing as an anti-fraud mechanism in procurement is contingent not merely on the existence of reporting channels, but on the credibility of protection afforded to reporters, the independence of investigative follow-through, and the broader ethical climate of the organisation. The paper concludes with a set of policy and managerial recommendations for strengthening whistleblowing systems within procurement functions, particularly in public sector and developing-economy contexts where institutional safeguards are often weakest.

title: Mapping Maqāṣid al-Sharī‘ah Research in Indonesia’s Digital Business: Trends, Domains, and Future Research Agenda
summary: The rapid development of digital business in Indonesia has encouraged the growing use of maqāṣid al-syarī'ah in Islamic economics research, yet the development, methodological quality, and conceptual orientation of this literature remain insufficiently mapped. This study examines publication trends, digital-business domains, methodological characteristics, maqāṣid al-syarī'ah dimensions, and research gaps in nationally accredited SINTA journals published between 2022 and 2026. A structured literature review was conducted using systematic search, screening, critical appraisal, and descriptive content analysis procedures. Literature was identified through GARUDA and Google Scholar, while journal accreditation was verified through the official SINTA portal. Seven studies satisfied the eligibility criteria and were included in the final synthesis. The literature is concentrated in digital marketing and Sharia fintech/e-wallets, each represented by two studies, while e-commerce, digital economic empowerment, and the digital economy are represented by one study each. Methodological appraisal indicates heterogeneous evidentiary strength and uneven reporting quality across empirical and library-based studies. In terms of maqāṣid dimensions, ḥifẓ al-māl appears in all seven studies (100.0%), while ḥifẓ al-dīn, ḥifẓ al-nafs, ḥifẓ al-'aql, and ḥifẓ al-nasl each appear in five studies (71.4%). Contrary to the initial coding, ḥifẓ al-bi'ah is explicitly incorporated in one study (14.3%), whereas ḥifẓ al-ummah is not explicitly operationalized. The principal research gap is therefore not the complete absence of contemporary maqāṣid, but their limited and uneven integration across digital-business research.

title: Designing Model Context Protocol Servers for SAP: Patterns for Secure, Governed Artificial Intelligence Access to SAP Data
summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is emerging as an open standard for connecting artificial intelligence agents to enterprise data sources and tool ecosystems. In SAP environments, where data governance, multi-tenant security, and regulatory compliance impose non-negotiable architectural constraints, deploying MCP servers requires design patterns that extend substantially beyond the protocol's reference implementation. This paper presents a systematic taxonomy of three MCP deployment patterns for SAP: a governed API gateway pattern via SAP Integration Suite, a custom server pattern on SAP Business Technology Platform, and a cross-cloud federated pattern using BTP Connectivity Service as a trust bridge. For each pattern, the authentication chain, design principles for the tool schema, and governance instrumentation required for production deployment are specified. The multi-hop authentication chain is introduced as a formally composable security property and demonstrated across all three patterns. A minimum viable governance framework of four components, tool registry, invocation audit logging, tool versioning and change management, and rate limiting with cost governance, is proposed as a reusable artifact for enterprise MCP deployments. A qualitative case study of the SAP Profit and Loss Advisor illustrates the practical realization of these patterns in a production financial reporting context. The contributions establish a foundation for governed, auditable AI access to SAP enterprise data that is reproducible across deployment contexts

summary: Existing digital payment systems fail to provide transparent akad documentation, integrated transaction evidence, and auditable financial records for halal MSMEs. Research Objective: to examine how blockchain-based transaction media improves akad transparency, financial governance, accountability, and transaction documentation in halal MSMEs locally. Methodology: a qualitative multiple-case study involving two halal MSMEs, using observations, semi-structured interviews, document reviews, transaction mapping, and thematic within-case and cross-case analyses to evaluate blockchain implementation outcomes. The findings indicate that transaction inefficiencies resulted primarily from fragmented documentation rather than inadequate digital payment technologies. Blockchain-based transaction media integrated akad details, payment confirmations, document hashes, timestamps, and verification records into a unified audit trail. This integration strengthened transaction transparency, improved financial accountability, enhanced the accuracy of daily reconciliations, and facilitated receivable monitoring. The system also simplified dispute verification by providing immutable transaction evidence. However, implementation challenges included limited user digital literacy, challenges in ensuring off-chain data validity, usability concerns, and implementation costs. Overall, blockchain functioned effectively as an accountability layer, complementing existing payment platforms rather than replacing familiar digital payment methods. Conclusion: Blockchain effectively strengthens transparency and governance when implemented as a simple accountability layer supporting existing digital payment infrastructures. The study offers practical evidence, readiness modeling, and locally grounded guidance for adopting blockchain-enabled Sharia fintech in halal MSMEs.

title: Collaborative Sustainability: Driving India’s Electric Two-Wheeler Market Through Vendor Synergy
summary: As the electric two-wheeler (E2W) sector rapidly proliferates in India, achieving genuine sustainability is strongly dependent upon upstream supply chain dynamics. Drawing on sustainable supply chain and partnership theories, this research investigates how strategic vendor partnerships (SVP) drive economic, environmental, and social sustainability within this emerging market. We deconstruct the SVP framework into three fundamental practices: outsourcing, vendor-managed inventory (VMI), and vendor selection tied to long-term alliances (VSLTA). For an evaluation of how these practices impact critical sustainability metrics like emission control, waste reduction, resource optimization, cost efficiency, and delivery reliability, we surveyed procurement and supply chain experts from major Indian E2W manufacturers and their tier-1 suppliers. The gathered data was empirically evaluated utilizing exploratory factor analysis and multiple regression. The analysis reveals that sustainable performance is significantly and positively enhanced by all three facets of SVP. Notably, establishing enduring relationships through VSLTA, proved to be the most impactful catalyst for sustainability, followed closely by VMI integration and outsourcing strategies. Finally, this research advances the academic discourse on sustainable e-mobility operations in developing economies and equips industry managers with evidence-based strategies to build supply chains that are both highly competitive and ecologically responsible.

title: Financial Technology Adoption and Performance of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) In Nairobi County, Kenya
summary: Abstract : Financial Technology (Fintech) has emerged as an important enabler of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (MSME) performance by improving access to financial services, enhancing operational efficiency, and strengthening business competitiveness. Despite the rapid expansion of Fintech services in Kenya, empirical evidence on how different dimensions of Fintech adoption influence MSME performance and how contextual factors shape this relationship remains limited. This study examined the effect of Financial Technology adoption on the performance of MSMEs in Nairobi County, Kenya. Specifically, it assessed the effects of Mobile Payment Platforms, Digital Lending Platforms, Digital Financial Management Tools, and Digital Market Platforms on MSME performance and examined the moderating effects of Digital Literacy, Trust and Security Concerns, and Internet Access. The study was anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model, Innovation Diffusion Theory, and Resource-Based View. A descriptive cross-sectional survey design was adopted, targeting 1,000 registered MSMEs in Nairobi County. Using Yamane’s formula, a sample of 286 MSMEs was determined and selected through stratified random sampling. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to MSME owners and managers. Of the 286 questionnaires distributed, 201 were successfully completed, yielding a 70.3% response rate. Data were analyzed using SPSS Version 27 through descriptive statistics, Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation, and Hierarchical Moderated Multiple Regression. The findings established that all four Fintech dimensions had positive and statistically significant effects on MSME performance. Mobile Payment Platforms recorded the strongest effect (β = 0.382, p < 0.001), followed by Digital Market Platforms (β = 0.301, p < 0.001), Digital Lending Platforms (β = 0.244, p < 0.001), and Digital Financial Management Tools (β = 0.118, p = 0.045). Collectively, the four dimensions explained 55.1% of the variation in MSME performance (R² = 0.551). Incorporating the moderating variables increased the explanatory power to 64.7% (R² = 0.647), representing an additional 9.6% variance explained. The study concludes that Fintech adoption significantly enhances MSME performance and that Digital Literacy, Trust and Security Concerns, and Internet Access strengthen this relationship. It recommends strengthening digital infrastructure, affordable internet access, digital literacy, cybersecurity, and consumer protection while encouraging financial institutions and Fintech providers to develop secure, affordable, and MSME-oriented solutions.

title: Public Accounting Reforms and Financial Management of Federal Government Agencies in Nigeria
summary: Scant empirical studies on public accounting reforms and financial management of federal government agencies necessitated the need to examine the relationship between public accounting reforms and financial management of federal government agencies in Nigeria. The population of the study comprised 90 federal government agencies, and a census approach was adopted due to the relatively small size of the population. Primary data were collected using a well-structured questionnaire anchored on a five-point Likert scale. A total of 240 copies of the questionnaire were distributed, out of which 209 were retrieved and used for analysis. The Pearson Product Moment Correlation Coefficient was employed to test the formulated hypotheses using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 21. The findings revealed that the Treasury Single Account has a significant relationship with public expenditure management of federal government agencies in Nigeria. Empirical evidence also showed that the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System has a significant relationship with public expenditure management. Furthermore, the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System was found to have a significant relationship with public expenditure management. The study concluded that public accounting reforms have significantly improved financial management in federal government agencies in Nigeria. The study recommended, among others, that the government should strengthen the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System to fully integrate budgetary processes. Federal government agencies should be mandated to fully adopt the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System to enhance transparency and accountability. Additionally, all government agencies should be enrolled in the Treasury Single Account to reduce financial leakages. The adoption of technological infrastructure such as biometric verification systems is also recommended to improve efficiency in financial management. Government should strengthen internal control mechanisms and risk management systems to curb financial mismanagement and corruption.

title: Cloud Accounting Adoption and Financial Performance of Small and Medium Enterprises in Nigeria
summary: This study investigates the effect of cloud accounting adoption on the financial performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria. SMEs contribute significantly to employment generation and economic development, yet many face challenges related to financial management, operational inefficiencies, and limited access to real-time financial information. Cloud accounting has emerged as an innovative technological solution capable of improving financial management through automation, remote accessibility, and enhanced data processing capabilities. This study adopted a survey research design using primary data collected through structured questionnaires administered to staff of SMEs operating in Asaba, Delta State, Nigeria. The population of the study consisted of 552 SMEs registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission and operating within the study area. Using Yamane’s sampling technique and purposive sampling, 40 respondents from eight SMEs that had adopted cloud accounting systems were selected for analysis. Data collected were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation coefficient and simple linear regression to examine the relationship between cloud accounting and financial performance indicators proxied by cash flow management, profitability, cost effectiveness, efficiency, and financial sustainability. The findings reveal that cloud accounting significantly improves cash flow monitoring, profitability, and efficiency among SMEs. The results further show that cloud accounting has a positive but relatively weaker relationship with cost effectiveness, while its impact on long-term financial sustainability was negative. The study concludes that cloud accounting plays a critical role in improving financial management and overall performance of SMEs in Nigeria. It recommends that SME owners adopt cloud-based accounting solutions and that policymakers support digital accounting adoption through training programs, incentives, and infrastructure development. These measures will enhance financial performance, and efficiency within Nigeria’s SME sector.

title: GREEN ACCOUNTING PRACTICES AND SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH: AN EMPIRICAL STUDY IN KANNIYAKUMARI DISTRICT
summary: Green accounting has emerged as an important approach for integrating environmental considerations into conventional accounting and business decision-making. Growing environmental concerns, regulatory expectations and stakeholder pressure have encouraged organizations to identify, measure and report their environmental costs and benefits. Green accounting practices enable businesses to assess resource consumption, waste management, energy efficiency, environmental expenditure and sustainability performance. The present study examines the relationship between green accounting practices and sustainable business growth among selected business organizations in Kanniyakumari District. The study adopts a descriptive and empirical research design and proposes the collection of primary data from business organizations through a structured questionnaire. Green accounting practices are examined through dimensions such as environmental cost identification, environmental reporting, energy management, waste management, resource efficiency and sustainable investment. Sustainable business growth is assessed through economic performance, operational efficiency, environmental performance, stakeholder satisfaction and long-term competitiveness. Percentage analysis, mean, standard deviation, Chi-square, correlation, ANOVA and multiple regression are used as proposed analytical tools. The model findings indicate a positive relationship between green accounting practices and sustainable business growth. The study recommends greater awareness, transparent environmental reporting, adoption of resource-efficient technologies and integration of environmental costs into managerial decision-making.

title: Sustainable Development Goals achievement and country development level - a three-dimensional analysis
summary: This study examines the nexus between the degree of implementation of SDGs across three dimensions: Society, Environment, and Good Governance and the achieved level of economic development in EU countries. Using the TOPSIS method, measures of sustainable development were constructed based on SDG and World Bank data for 2013 and 2023. Correlation analysis was used to compare the relationship between economic development and the three ESG dimensions. While most countries have improved their economic performance and environmental indicators, almost all have experienced a decline in social indicators. Of the areas identified, only a positive correlation was found between the economy and society. Governance factors showed strong correlations with economic development only in 2013. The research reveals that economic growth alone does not guarantee sustainability across ESG factors. Policymakers must adopt integrated strategies coordinating economic, social, environmental, and governance policies simultaneously to ensure sustainable development. This study fills a research gap by providing a comprehensive three-dimensional ESG analysis of SDG implementation levels relative to economic development.

title: Sustainability Reporting in Extractive Industries: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Agenda
summary: ABSTRACT This study provides a systematic and integrative review of ESG and sustainability reporting in extractive industries, aiming to assess the current state of the literature and identify key theoretical, methodological, and contextual gaps. Given the growing importance of extractive sectors in supporting global sustainability transitions, understanding the role of ESG reporting as a governance mechanism is increasingly critical. The review adopts a domain‐based approach combining bibliometric mapping, thematic analysis, and content‐based classification. A dataset of 106 peer‐reviewed articles (2000–2025) was analysed using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer, alongside a structured coding framework based on theoretical, contextual, and methodological dimensions. The findings reveal a rapidly expanding but still fragmented research field. From a theoretical perspective, the literature remains predominantly anchored in traditional frameworks such as stakeholder and legitimacy theories, while a fully integrated ESG and governance‐oriented perspective is still emerging. Methodologically, the field shows a prevalence of quantitative approaches, although these are predominantly applied in descriptive and exploratory ways. The results also highlight a strong imbalance across ESG dimensions, with environmental issues receiving significantly greater attention than social and governance aspects. In addition, the literature is geographically concentrated in developed economies, with emerging and resource‐intensive regions underrepresented. A central contribution of this study lies in identifying a structural misalignment between academic research and ongoing regulatory developments. While the literature continues to emphasise voluntary disclosure practices, the global reporting landscape is increasingly shaped by mandatory and standardised frameworks. This transition redefines sustainability reporting from a legitimacy‐driven communication tool to a formalised governance mechanism, although its effectiveness in driving substantive sustainability performance remains uncertain. Overall, this study aims to contribute to the literature by providing a comprehensive mapping of ESG reporting research in extractive industries and by advancing an interpretative framework that highlights its evolving role within sustainability transitions. The findings offer relevant insights for scholars, policymakers, and practitioners, and outline key directions for future research aimed at strengthening the theoretical and empirical foundations of the field.

title: From Fear to Fluency: Cultivating AI Confidence and Socio-Economic Wellbeing in the Workforce
summary: Industry 5.0 emphasises human-centric, sustainable, and resilient digital transformation, in which technology augments human skills and wellbeing. While the integration of generative AI into workplaces is rapidly reshaping job roles, this study investigates how organisations can guide employees from AI-related fear to fluency, achieving confident, ethical, and psychologically safe engagement with AI systems, and proposes a contextualised diagnostic tool for measuring organisational readiness. A mixed-methods design was used. Quantitatively, 217 professionals from AI-adopting organisations completed a nine-item online survey measuring psychological safety, innovation climate, skill confidence, leadership communication, policy understanding, training efficacy, and adoption outcomes, analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations. Qualitatively, 15 semi-structured interviews with mid-level managers across French, Indian, and American operating contexts were deductively coded against six a priori dimensions and triangulated against the survey findings. Qualitative accounts converged with quantitative patterns on the centrality of leadership translation and the insufficiency of generic training, while showing partial divergence on how explicitly managers themselves name psychological safety as a lever. The study finally proposes the AI Readiness Scan, a six-dimension diagnostic (psychological safety, intercultural contextualisation, regulatory compliance, skill confidence, change resilience, and leadership AI readiness), each grounded in an established measurement or theoretical literature, to help organisations act on evidence rather than assumption before and during AI transformation. The findings bridge psychological safety theory, responsible AI governance, and international labour considerations into an integrated, actionable framework for managers and policymakers navigating AI-driven digital transformation.

title: Architecting Resilient Big Data Lakehouse Pipelines for Emerging Market Digital Retail: Mitigating Sizing Returns, Payment Drop-offs, and Logistics Volatility
summary: Digital retail platforms in emerging sub-Saharan African economies face unique systemic bottlenecks that undermine operating margins and erode customer lifetime value. Unlike mature Western e-commerce ecosystems, emerging market merchants encounter high payment gateway timeout rates (25% to 30%), severe reverse logistics costs driven by apparel sizing discrepancies (apparel returns exceeding 40%), and volatile supply chain lead times. While Enterprise Architecture (EA) and Big Data Lakehouse paradigms have been extensively explored in high-infrastructure environments, their architectural contextualization for high-latency, network-constrained emerging retail operations remains under-researched. This paper introduces the Resilient Emerging Retail Lakehouse Architecture (RERLA), an integrated data engineering and predictive machine learning framework designed specifically for developing economy commerce. RERLA combines decentralized Data Mesh domain ownership with a 4-layer Lakehouse stack powered by Apache Kafka event streaming, Delta Lake ACID parquet storage, and low-latency microservice serving layers. To mitigate operational friction, RERLA implements dual specialized machine learning inference pipelines: (1) a multi-variable Random Forest classifier analyzing ordinal fit perceptions and continuous dwell telemetry to deliver proactive sizing advisories, and (2) a real-time gradient-boosted payment router predicting gateway failure propensity and triggering instant fallback rails. Evaluated across a large-scale synthetic benchmark of 50,000 multi-channel retail transactions modeling Nigerian e-commerce dynamics, RERLA demonstrates significant operational performance: reducing product return rates by 43.44% (from 46.01% to 26.02%), recovering 52.56% of failed payment conversions (lowering gateway abandonment from 27.68% to 13.13%), and maintaining sub-15ms inference latency across distributed edge nodes. This research provides a reproducible technical blueprint and empirical foundation for enterprise decision systems in emerging digital economies.
